_comment: Version 2 is a separately versioned regional topic vocabulary; v1 remains immutable.
Includes one new subject: military humanitarian assistance and disaster response.
Do not bulk-convert v1 proposals, China local categories, or shadow records.
Every applied assignment requires an explicitly opted-in store and recorded provenance.

groups.description: Military activity, posture, access, and operational competition.
Intergovernmental and military relationships, agreements, and cooperative activity.
Acquisition, industrial capacity, strategic capabilities, and enabling technologies.
Geographically bounded security questions that recur across multiple desks.
Economic instruments, supply chains, and controls with security implications.
Formal or semi-formal concepts about strategy, doctrine, force employment, and planning.

topics.description: Exercises, drills, training events, readiness activity, and combined or joint training.
topics.scope_note: Use for an identifiable training or exercise event. Routine operations without a training purpose belong elsewhere.

topics.description: Military involvement in humanitarian assistance, civilian disaster response, rescue, relief logistics, evacuation, and mission-specific preparedness.
topics.scope_note: Use when military or armed-police civilian-relief operations, directly tasked support expenditure, or dedicated HADR training are substantive. Exclude generic goodwill, civilian healthcare, troop welfare, unrelated medical care, and disasters mentioned only as background. HADR does not imply procurement or defense diplomacy.

topics.description: Deployments, rotations, access arrangements, bases, ports, facilities, and persistent force posture.
topics.scope_note: Use for a substantively discussed deployment, rotation, access arrangement, or force location. Temporary operational port access may qualify; a venue name or base mentioned incidentally does not establish basing.

topics.description: Naval and maritime security activity, sea-lane protection, maritime domain awareness, and maritime incidents.
topics.scope_note: Geographic disputes may also receive a flashpoint topic. Coast-guard or coercive gray-zone activity may also receive gray_zone_coast_guard.

topics.description: Coast-guard operations, maritime law-enforcement coercion, militia activity, and sub-threshold military pressure.
topics.scope_note: Use for coercive or security-relevant activity below conventional armed conflict; do not apply to routine civilian enforcement without a security dimension.

topics.description: Defense-ministry, military-to-military, senior-official, and institutional diplomatic engagement.
topics.scope_note: Use for substantive defense or military engagement. Civilian police cooperation and ceremonials do not automatically qualify; verify the defense-institution and engagement nexus.

topics.description: Alliance commitments, defense agreements, security partnerships, access frameworks, and recurring cooperative mechanisms.
topics.scope_note: Use for a durable defense/security relationship, explicit agreement, access framework or recurring cooperation mechanism. Ordinary agenda lists, co-mention, and standalone police contact do not establish an alliance or security partnership.

topics.description: Purchases, tenders, acquisition programs, deliveries, upgrades, sustainment decisions, and capability procurement.
topics.scope_note: Require a concrete acquisition, contracted purchase, upgrade or sustainment decision. A military HADR support budget, routine exercise or equipment affiliation alone does not imply procurement.

topics.description: Defense production, industrial-base capacity, co-production, shipbuilding, munitions capacity, and defense-sector investment.
topics.scope_note: Use when production capacity, firms, industrial policy, or manufacturing is substantively discussed.

topics.description: Artificial intelligence, autonomy, quantum, advanced sensing, uncrewed systems, and other emerging defense technologies.
topics.scope_note: Require materially developed military or explicitly security-linked emerging technology, not a bare organization name, agenda mention, generic modernization, or incidental civilian AI. A public-security application needs a concrete security-technology mechanism.

topics.description: Nuclear forces, nuclear posture, extended deterrence, strategic weapons, and nuclear command or signaling.
topics.scope_note: Use for nuclear-specific capability, posture, policy, or signaling.

topics.description: Cyber operations, information warfare, influence operations, electronic warfare, and information-domain capabilities.
topics.scope_note: Use for substantive security-relevant cyber operations or defense, military information systems, influence/information operations, and electronic warfare. A brief cooperation agenda, press release, ordinary electronic communications, or crime mention does not by itself qualify. No inference of a cyberattack from networks or cybersecurity alone.

topics.description: Military and security space systems, counterspace activity, space-domain awareness, launches, and space cooperation.
topics.scope_note: Require substantive military/security-linked space capability, institution, operation, counterspace measure, military reconnaissance, or space-domain policy. Exclude routine civil launches, general astronaut stories, and affiliation alone without developed space-security substance.

topics.description: Cross-strait security, Taiwan-related military posture, coercion, deterrence, and contingency planning.
topics.scope_note: This regional topic is distinct from the China Desk's legacy category slug taiwan; no automatic equivalence is implied.

topics.description: Security activity, disputes, operations, coercion, and defense policy tied materially to the South China Sea.
topics.scope_note: Use only when the South China Sea is a substantive subject, not merely a geographic transit reference.

topics.description: Security activity, disputes, operations, and defense policy tied materially to the East China Sea.
topics.scope_note: Require a substantive East China Sea security dispute, coercive event, regional posture or policy, including dispute-linked action around the Diaoyu/Senkaku islands. A naval exercise merely located in the East China Sea does not suffice.

topics.description: Economic policy explicitly linked to national security, resilience, strategic dependency, or defense preparedness.
topics.scope_note: Use for security-linked economic policy. Ordinary trade or macroeconomic policy is out of scope.

topics.description: Export controls, sanctions, investment restrictions, technology controls, and related coercive economic measures.
topics.scope_note: Use when a specific restriction, listing, licensing measure, sanction, technology control or concrete formally proposed control is materially discussed. Mere announcements of possible pressure, generic sanction rhetoric, advisories without restriction, and unrelated tax measures are insufficient.

topics.description: Critical minerals, strategic materials, security-relevant supply dependence, stockpiles, and defense-related industrial supply resilience.
topics.scope_note: Use for concrete strategic materials, minerals, stockpiles, defense-relevant supply dependencies or security-linked industrial supply resilience. An explicit security/dependency nexus is required; do not infer minerals when only broader supply resilience is discussed. Generic supplier or agenda mentions are insufficient.

topics.description: Doctrine, strategic concepts, operational concepts, force-employment theory, and formal strategic planning.
topics.scope_note: Require a substantive strategic or operational concept, force-employment framework, or doctrine—not a routine speech or readiness slogan. Multi-topic records require independent subject-specific passages.
